title: Examination of a neck lump (not thyroid)

guidelineVersions: UK head and neck cancer guidelines, 6th edition (2024)

related.why: Feeling for pulsatility and listening for a bruit

brief.setting: ENT and head and neck outpatient clinic
brief.scenario: Mr Owen Penhaligon, 29, a PE teacher who has never smoked, noticed a painless swelling on the left side of his neck six weeks ago. It got bigger for a few days during a sore throat last month. His GP referred him on the suspected cancer pathway.
brief.task: Examine his neck. You will be stopped at 6 minutes to present your findings and answer questions.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Look, feel from behind, nodes and salivary glands, mouth and throat; then the investigation plan.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Calling it a branchial cyst and forgetting a cystic node.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "Could you undo your top buttons so I can see your whole neck, down to your collarbones?"

flow: Introduce, consent, expose to the clavicles

grid.label: Preparation and position
grid.fail: Palpates from the front without exposing the neck.
grid.pass: Introduces, confirms identity, gains consent, cleans hands, exposes the neck to the clavicles, and sits him upright.
grid.high: Asks him to point to the lump and whether it's tender before touching, and has a glass of water ready.

grid.label: Inspection
grid.pass: Inspects from the front and side for site, size, skin changes and scars; asks him to swallow and to stick out his tongue.
grid.high: Places the lump in the anterior triangle at the anterior border of the sternocleidomastoid, junction of upper and middle thirds.

grid.label: Palpation of the lump
grid.pass: From behind: size, shape, surface, consistency, tenderness, warmth, fluctuation, mobility and relation to the sternocleidomastoid; feels for pulsation and listens for a bruit.
grid.high: Notes whether it moves side to side but not up and down (carotid body mass pattern), and whether it lies deep to the muscle.

grid.label: Lymph nodes and salivary glands
grid.pass: Palpates every node group on both sides in order, then the parotid and submandibular glands, bimanually for the submandibular.
grid.high: Checks facial nerve function with any parotid swelling, and offers axillae, groins, liver and spleen if lymphoma is possible.

grid.label: Mouth and throat
grid.pass: Examines the mouth, tongue, floor of mouth and tonsils with a light and tongue depressor, and offers flexible nasendoscopy.
grid.high: States that anyone with cervical lymphadenopathy needs fibre-optic nasopharyngolaryngoscopy.

grid.label: Presentation at the signal
grid.fail: Describes the lump but gives no differential.
grid.pass: Presents a structured description and a differential: branchial cyst, lymph node (reactive, lymphoma, metastasis), salivary or carotid body mass.
grid.high: Leads with 'a smooth fluctuant lump at the anterior border of the sternocleidomastoid: likely branchial cyst', then says a cystic node must be excluded.

grid.label: Investigation
grid.fail: Plans to excise the 'cyst' without imaging or a needle biopsy.
grid.pass: Arranges ultrasound with ultrasound-guided FNAC or core biopsy in a neck lump clinic, and nasendoscopy.
grid.high: Knows core biopsy suits suspected lymphoma or salivary tumours, the cyst wall should be targeted, and open biopsy is a last resort.

grid.label: Suspected cancer pathway (safety-critical)
grid.fail: Reassures and discharges him because he is young and a non-smoker.
grid.pass: Says he meets the NG12 criteria for a persistent unexplained neck lump and stays on the suspected cancer pathway (28 days).
grid.high: Keeps NICE's wording: 'consider' referral for a persistent unexplained neck lump at any age (oral), or an unexplained neck lump at 45 and over (laryngeal).

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: [From the front, collar still done up.] Let me feel it.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: There's a lump on the left. [Doesn't describe it; doesn't feel other nodes or glands.]

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I've finished. [Doesn't look in the mouth.]

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Book him for excision. He's young and doesn't smoke, so cancer is unlikely.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Hello, I'm Dr Sandhu, one of the surgical trainees. Can I check your name and date of birth? I'd like to examine your neck. Could you undo your top buttons? [Consent; cleans hands.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Inspects front and side.] Could you swallow this water? Now stick out your tongue. [The lump doesn't move.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I'll feel from behind. [Describes size, shape, surface, consistency, fluctuation, mobility; relation to the sternocleidomastoid; feels for pulsation; listens for a bruit.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Feels every node group on both sides in order, then the parotid glands and, bimanually, the submandibular glands.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Could you open wide? [Light and tongue depressor: tongue, floor of mouth, tonsils.] I'd also like a flexible nasendoscopy. Thank you. [Cleans hands.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Mr Penhaligon has a 4 by 3 centimetre smooth, fluctuant, non-tender lump at the anterior border of the left sternocleidomastoid. It doesn't move on swallowing, isn't pulsatile, and there are no other nodes. The differential is a branchial cyst or a lymph node: reactive, lymphoma or metastasis.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Ultrasound with ultrasound-guided FNAC or core biopsy in the neck lump clinic, and nasendoscopy.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Does he need to be on a cancer pathway?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Yes. He meets the NG12 criteria for a persistent unexplained neck lump and stays on the suspected cancer pathway, 28 days.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Hello, I'm Dr Sandhu, one of the surgical trainees. Can I check your name and date of birth? Could you point to the lump? Is it sore? I'll need your whole neck uncovered, and I have some water here. [Cleans hands.]

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Inspects.] Anterior triangle, at the anterior border of the sternocleidomastoid, junction of its upper and middle thirds. It doesn't move on swallowing or tongue protrusion, so it isn't thyroid or thyroglossal.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [From behind.] Smooth, oval, fluctuant, partly deep to the muscle. It moves freely in both directions and isn't pulsatile, so not the pattern of a carotid body mass. No bruit.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Nodes, parotids, submandibular glands.] No other nodes. Facial nerve intact. With lymphoma in the differential I'd examine the axillae, groins, liver and spleen.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Mouth and tonsils normal.] Anyone with a neck node needs fibre-optic nasendoscopy, so I'd do that too. [Cleans hands.]

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Mr Penhaligon has a smooth fluctuant lump at the anterior border of the left sternocleidomastoid, most likely a branchial cyst. A cystic lymph node must be excluded. No other nodes; mouth and salivary glands normal.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Same-day ultrasound with a guided biopsy, targeting the cyst wall; core biopsy if lymphoma is suspected. I wouldn't excise it until the cytology is back: open biopsy is a last resort.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Does he need to be on a cancer pathway?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: NICE says consider a suspected cancer pathway referral for a persistent unexplained neck lump at any age; the laryngeal criterion is 45 and over. He meets the first, so he stays on the 28-day pathway.

failures.move: Examining the lump without the other nodes or salivary glands.
failures.consequence: Multiple nodes or a salivary source are missed, and the differential is wrong.

failures.move: Not examining the mouth and throat.
failures.consequence: A primary tumour, the source of a nodal metastasis, is missed.

failures.move: Excising a presumed branchial cyst without a needle biopsy.
failures.consequence: A cystic SCC metastasis is opened in the neck, complicating later treatment.

failures.move: Discharging a young non-smoker with a persistent neck lump.
failures.consequence: Safety-critical: lymphoma and HPV-related cancer are not excluded.

recovery.line: Before I finish, could you take a sip of water and then stick out your tongue?

recovery.when: The examiner asks if it could be malignant
recovery.line: Yes: a cystic node from an oropharyngeal cancer can look like a branchial cyst, so I'd get a guided biopsy first.

knowledge.fact: Neck node: fibre-optic nasendoscopy; same-day ultrasound and guided FNAC or core biopsy; open biopsy is a last resort.
Many lateral cystic neck masses over 40 are metastatic HPV-related oropharyngeal SCC.
Nodal SCC with unknown primary: consider FDG PET-CT first.
NG12: consider referral for a persistent unexplained neck lump (oral), an unexplained neck lump at 45 and over (laryngeal), or unexplained lymphadenopathy (lymphoma).
Suspected paraganglioma: MRI, plasma metanephrines and a specialist centre.

recall.think: Is this a cystic node from a cancer, or lymphoma?
recall.say: "Likely branchial cyst, but a cystic node must be excluded."

numbers.meaning: lateral cystic neck mass: often malignant

recall.trap: A young non-smoker with a 'branchial cyst' can have lymphoma or HPV-related cancer.
recall.finish: Ultrasound-guided biopsy before any excision of a presumed branchial cyst.

sources.name: ICBSE Guide to the intercollegiate MRCS examination
sources.supports: Introduce yourself, confirm identity, obtain consent and clean hands at every station; 6-minute signal in examination stations

sources.name: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery (O'Connell, McCaskie, Sayers, eds)
sources.supports: Neck examination technique: from behind, swallowing and tongue protrusion, node groups, salivary glands; branchial cyst position at the anterior border of the sternocleidomastoid; carotid body mass mobility

sources.name: NICE NG12: Suspected cancer: recognition and referral
sources.supports: Consider a suspected cancer pathway referral for laryngeal cancer at 45 and over with persistent unexplained hoarseness or an unexplained lump in the neck (1.8.1); consider a suspected cancer pathway referral for oral cancer with unexplained oral ulceration for more than 3 weeks or a persistent and unexplained lump in the neck (1.8.2); consider referral for thyroid cancer with an unexplained thyroid lump (1.8.5); consider referral for non-Hodgkin (1.10.6) or Hodgkin lymphoma (1.10.8) in adults with unexplained lymphadenopathy, taking into account fever, night sweats, shortness of breath, pruritus, weight loss or alcohol-induced node pain; suspected cancer pathway: diagnosis or ruling out of cancer within 28 days of referral

sources.name: NICE NG36: Cancer of the upper aerodigestive tract: assessment and management in people aged 16 or over
sources.supports: Consider adding ultrasound guidance to FNAC or core biopsy for a neck lump suspected of being upper aerodigestive tract cancer (1.2.1); consider FDG PET-CT as the first investigation to find the primary in metastatic nodal SCC of unknown origin (1.2.3)

sources.name: Homer JJ, et al. Head and Neck Cancer: United Kingdom National Multidisciplinary Guidelines, Sixth Edition. J Laryngol Otol 2024;138(S1):S1–S224
sources.version: Sixth edition; published online 14 March 2024 (issue April 2024)
sources.supports: Chapter 2: patients with cervical lymphadenopathy require fibre-optic nasopharyngolaryngoscopy (R); a neck lump clinic should include same-day ultrasound and ultrasound-guided FNAC or core biopsy (G); core biopsy may be more accurate than FNAC for suspected lymphoma and salivary gland tumours; many lateral cystic neck masses in patients over 40 prove to be malignant, most commonly metastatic HPV-associated SCC from an oropharyngeal primary; target the cyst wall; open biopsy should be a last resort. Chapter 30: suspected paraganglioma: MRI, plasma metanephrines, referral to a specialist centre

partner.opening: Please examine this patient's neck. I'll stop you at 6 minutes.
partner.actorBrief: You are Mr Owen Penhaligon, 29, a PE teacher who has never smoked. You noticed a painless swelling on the left of your neck six weeks ago while shaving. It swelled for a few days during a sore throat last month, then settled. No weight loss, night sweats, itching, hoarseness or swallowing problems. You're worried because a colleague had lymphoma; say so only if asked how you feel about it.

reveals.trigger: Inspects; asks him to swallow and protrude the tongue
reveals.finding: Left-sided swelling about 4 × 3 cm at the anterior border of the sternocleidomastoid, junction of upper and middle thirds. Normal skin, no scars. Doesn't move with swallowing or tongue protrusion.
Smooth, oval, soft and fluctuant, non-tender, not warm. Partly deep to the sternocleidomastoid. Mobile in all directions. Not pulsatile; no bruit.
No other palpable nodes, including supraclavicular. Parotid and submandibular glands normal. Facial nerve intact.
Oral cavity, tongue, floor of mouth and tonsils normal and symmetrical.
Say: "Thank you; assume these are normal."
Say: "Please stop there and present your findings."

push.question: What is your differential diagnosis?
push.expect: Branchial cyst; lymph node (reactive, lymphoma, cystic metastasis); less likely salivary or carotid body mass.

push.question: How would you investigate?
push.expect: Nasendoscopy; ultrasound with ultrasound-guided FNAC or core biopsy in a neck lump clinic; core biopsy if lymphoma suspected.

push.question: Is he on a suspected cancer pathway?
push.expect: Yes: he meets NG12 criteria (persistent unexplained neck lump) and stays on the suspected cancer pathway (28 days).

curveballs.prompt: The same lump in a 52-year-old non-smoker.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Many lateral cystic neck masses over 40 are metastatic HPV-related oropharyngeal SCC: nasendoscopy and ultrasound-guided biopsy of the cyst wall; if nodal SCC with no primary, consider PET-CT first. Don't excise as a branchial cyst.

curveballs.prompt: The lump is pulsatile and moves side to side but not up and down.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Suspected carotid body paraganglioma: contrast MRI, plasma metanephrines, and referral to a specialist centre.

curveballs.prompt: He also has night sweats, weight loss and nodes in both sides of the neck.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Consider lymphoma (NG12 lymphadenopathy criteria); core biopsy rather than FNAC, plus examination of the other node areas, liver and spleen.

curveballs.prompt: The lump is in front of the ear, over the angle of the jaw.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Parotid mass: check facial nerve function; ultrasound-guided core biopsy.
